notes:
Fictional, complete-measurement whole cohort, not recovered individuals. This is one possible scientific law, not an estimate of the full Lea joint distribution. ANALYSIS: Generate raw BMI and lipids; downstream use a separate pooled sample mean and sample SD (ddof=1) for each outcome, never sex-specific or group-specific standardization. Conditional arithmetic means are linear in age, sex and lifestyle-by-sex, so age/sex-adjusted additive and all sex-specific contrasts can be estimated on that common scale; nonzero small interactions are retained rather than selected by significance. The 2-df Gaussian ML LRT remains a working-model analysis of mildly skewed, heteroscedastic observations; no p-value is forced. Source published contrasts used outcome-specific measured samples, including only 406 lipids. Completing all 1226 lipid measurements changes precision and may change detection; source nonsignificance is not an equivalence result.
DEMOGRAPHY: Fix stratified age-bin/sex/lifestyle counts by Hamilton largest-remainder allocation of the printed 1360 cells to n=1226, ties in printed order. This is a transparent design assumption, not a correction or demographic recovery. Uniform continuous ages within [18,31), [31,41), [41,51), [51,61), [61,70), [70,85), with the 18 endpoint excluded. Top bin deliberately interpreted as 70-inclusive with assumed cap 85, resolving but not claiming to explain printed age-70 ambiguity. Conditional age/sex means are centered at each lifestyle's analytic covariate means, not sample-fitted outcome values. Fixed stratum counts ensure all six sex/lifestyle groups are analysable; age and biomarkers remain stochastic.
NUMERICAL ORIGINS: Lea Results, traditional pastoralist section reports marginal pastoralist BMI 19.99 +/-2.14 and HDL 72.69 +/-14.72 (mean +/- individual SD). Only the pastoralist means/SDs are anchored to those statistics; never applied as pooled summaries. Urban BMI=19.99*1.0969=21.927031 and rural BMI=urban/1.0843 approximately20.2223, derived from Lea's descriptive 9.69% and 8.43% differences. Treating rounded descriptive percentages as marginal means, not standardized adjusted coefficients, is an approximation. Analytic removal of the assumed pastoralist age/sex mean variance from reported marginal variance gives the residual BMI and HDL SDs; generated sample moments naturally fluctuate. TC baseline148.58=72.69 HDL+60.89 published pastoralist LDL+15 assumed remnant cholesterol. This bookkeeping is a physiological assumption, not a recovered fasting Friedewald estimate. Rural/urban TC mean increments1.5/15 mg/dL and HDL increments -0.5/-1 mg/dL are explicitly assumed modest shifts consistent with, but not numerically identified by, source urban-TC elevation and undetected HDL contrasts. Rural BMI/TC/HDL effects are not fixed to zero.
UNSUPPORTED / PARTIALLY TRANSPORTED STRUCTURE: Age slopes BMI0.015 kg/m2/year, HDL0.03 and TC0.25 mg/dL/year are weak, shared-slope assumptions (not extracted regression estimates). Female effects at the reference age: BMI0.8 kg/m2, HDL3.87 mg/dL, TC2 mg/dL, with additional rural/urban female effects BMI0.1/0.2, HDL0.3/-0.8, TC0.5/1.5, all explicit small nonzero-effect assumptions. The external rural Kenya study motivates direction/scale only for BMI and HDL sex effects, not transport of adjusted coefficients. BMI residual multipliers1/1.05/1.30, non-HDL residual SD25/26/30 mg/dL, constant HDL residual scale, lognormal families and latent residual correlations (-0.15 BMI-HDL, +0.25 BMI-nonHDL, +0.10 HDL-nonHDL) are assumptions for heterogeneous adiposity, modest joint metabolic dependence, and positive concentrations. These are latent Gaussian correlations, not measured raw correlations. External TC SDs provide only a rough plausibility check on lipid spread; do not average external means with unusually high Turkana HDL. All moments are finite because ages are bounded, conditional mean/scale are bounded, and conditional innovations are lognormal. No empirical tail clipping, rescaling to a fitted contrast, rejection for statistical significance, or null-effect hard constraint is used. Source pastoralist absence of obesity is not a hard population bound.
PHYSIOLOGY / MEASUREMENT: TC=HDL+positive non-HDL guarantees HDL<TC; therefore no HDL-above-TC records exist by design, rather than being silently repaired. This models coherent concentrations; independent CardioChek error could violate that inequality in actual readings and is not reproduced. Units kg/m2 and mg/dL. Complete virtual biomarkers are a task choice, not 1226 new clinical observations or reproduction of original missingness. Parameters are held fixed across cohorts; individual sampling variation is not uncertainty about scientific evidence, and no probability is assigned to these uncertain modeling choices.

external.measurement: BMI kg/m2; overnight-fasting venous TC/HDL/LDL via standard assays in Denmark, mmol/L; different measurement conditions from Lea.
external.population_selection: 1084 rural Luo, Kamba and Maasai participants in 2005, including331 Maasai (170women/161men); eligibility >=17, nonpregnant, without specified illness/disability, complete metabolic/activity data. Separate from Lea2018-19 cohort; cannot be treated as same-population replication.
external.table1_operator: Unadjusted sex/ethnicity-specific mean (SD), not regression coefficient.
external.title: Physical activity energy expenditure and cardiometabolic health in three rural Kenyan populations
external.used_findings: Maasai BMI women22.5(4.8),men21.0(4.8); HDL women1.2(0.3),men1.1(0.32)mmol/L (female excess0.1*38.67=3.867mg/dL). Rural TC SD0.9-1.1mmol/L approximately34.8-42.5mg/dL used only as loose variability context. Absolute HDL means not transferred because Lea explicitly describes Turkana as unusually high.

primary.operators: Pastoralist descriptive mean/SD; descriptive BMI percentage comparisons; age/sex-adjusted standardized-outcome linear lifestyle comparisons and sex-interaction LRT. Exact S2 coefficients unavailable; not reconstructed or claimed.
primary.population_selection: Healthy self-reported Turkana ancestry adults >18, Kenya April2018-March2019; pregnancy/extreme biomarker outliers and missing key interview/demographic data excluded. Lifestyle county/subsistence definitions and EDTA/CardioChek measurement from supplied approved evidence.
